sections.html:
Property tax here runs through three desks at the Sevier County Courthouse, 125 Court Avenue, Sevierville. The Assessor decides what your property is worth, the County Commission picks the rate, and the Trustee sends the bill and takes payment. Match your question to the right desk and you skip a lot of stair climbing.

  • Property Assessor: Suite 210 West, 865.453.3242, open weekdays 8 a.m. to 4:30 p.m. Staff appraise and classify taxable property, and they redraw ownership and tax maps whenever a deed is recorded.
  • Trustee: Room 212W, (865) 453-2767, same hours. Enter by the west-end doors and turn right into the first office. A payment drop box stands behind the courthouse, where the 30 minute parking area meets West Bruce Street.
  • Clerk and Master: Suite 108 W, (865) 453-4654. Accounts that go delinquent end up here, along with the yearly tax sale auction.

Sevierville, Pigeon Forge and Gatlinburg lie within the county lines. Check with the city hall for your address to learn whether you also get a city bill.

Population stands at 101,342 as of July 2025, spread across 62,724 housing units. About 70.7% of households own their home, and owner-occupied homes carry a typical value of $299,000. Builders pulled 1,139 permits in 2025. Cabin rentals have multiplied around Gatlinburg and Pigeon Forge, so plenty of sellers own a nightly rental instead of a primary residence. The Assessor offers an online filing for nightly rentals, and the county website has a short-term rental tax estimator next to the primary home and vacant land estimators.

The formula has three steps: appraised value, times a state-mandated assessment ratio, times the local rate. Houses and farmland are assessed at one quarter of appraisal, while commercial and industrial land is assessed at 40 percent. Rates are quoted for each hundred dollars of assessed value, and the Trustee's FAQ showed $1.48 for 2024.

Values are reset every five years, and 2026 is a reappraisal year. The Assessor reviews roughly 90,000 parcels. A certified rate is then worked out under state law so that total collections hold steady, and the Board of Commissioners adopts the final figure. Some owners will pay more and some less, so read your own 2026 bill.

Between cycles your value stays fixed unless the building or land physically changes. Changing hands does not reset it.

Bills for 2026 went out in early October. You may pay any time from October 1 and owe no penalty until the end of February 2027. Past that point, 1.5 percent interest builds each month on the unpaid base amount. A mailed check must carry a postmark on or before the last day, and the Trustee will not accept an office meter date. Card and e-check payments count on the day you make them. You can pay in installments, and interest applies only to what is left.

Sevier County property tax calendar
DateWhat happens
January 1Assessment date for ownership, assessments and tax maps
March 1Business personal property schedules and greenbelt applications due
MayAssessment change notices mailed
June 1Board of Equalization opens appeal hearings
First week of OctoberTrustee mails bills; payable from October 1
End of FebruaryLast day to pay without interest

Mortgage companies do not get a copy from the Trustee, so if your lender escrows taxes, forward the bill. Each year's tax covers that calendar year.

Start with a call to the Assessor. If that goes nowhere, file with the Board of Equalization, which opens appeal hearings June 1. The reappraisal line is (865) 774-3756, answered weekday mornings and afternoons, and email goes to reappraisal@seviercountytn.gov.

Build your file first. Useful items are recent sales of comparable houses, contractor estimates for defects the appraisal overlooked, and corrections to square footage or condition. Ask what the filing deadline is this cycle, since notice dates shift. Begin when the May notice shows up, not when the bill does.

The Trustee runs two state programs for homeowners and fills out the application with you at the counter. Tax Relief pays all or part of the tax on a home, mobile homes included, for owners 65 or older, owners with disabilities, disabled former service members, and their widowed spouses. Posted limits for 2025 taxes:

  • Elderly and disabled owners: household income capped at $37,530 including a spouse, with relief figured on market value up to $32,700
  • Disabled former service members and surviving spouses: no income test, relief figured on market value up to $175,000
  • Tax Freeze, age 65 and up: income may not exceed $47,990 for 2024, and the application is renewed each year

Relief applies to city taxes as well. Greenbelt is a separate break for parcels of 15 acres or more in farm or forestry use, requested by March 1, and land that leaves the program owes a rollback of three years of savings. Confirm this year's limits with the Trustee before counting on any of these figures.

A tax lien stays with the parcel, so whatever is owed must be paid at or before closing. The Trustee bills whoever is listed as owner, and buyers are pointed to the closing statement to see who covers that year's tax. The title company normally pays an open balance at the table from your proceeds.

Once the deadline passes, the account is delinquent and goes to Chancery Court, where costs get added and the parcel may be advertised for the annual auction. The Clerk and Master posts the list 20 to 30 days before the sale. Bidders sign in at the courthouse 30 minutes before it begins and pay with cash, money order or check. The former owner can still redeem for a year, and the winning bidder earns 1 percent a month while waiting.

Owe back taxes? Phone the Trustee at (865) 453-2767 before your name reaches the list. A cash sale skips listing prep, showings and lender delays, so it can close fast enough to clear the balance ahead of the auction. Request a payoff figure near your closing date, since costs and interest keep growing.

faqs.q: Who mails the property tax bill in Sevier County?
faqs.a: Bills come from the Trustee, usually in the first week of October. Valuing is the Assessor's job and rate-setting belongs to the County Commission, but payment goes to the Trustee at 125 Court Avenue, Room 212W. If nothing arrives, call (865) 453-2767.

faqs.q: What is the deadline for paying Sevier County property tax without interest?
faqs.a: February's last day, which means February 2027 for the 2026 bill. From March 1, interest runs at 1.5 percent a month (18 percent a year), and a postmark after the deadline is treated as late.

faqs.q: Can I pay Sevier County property tax in pieces?
faqs.a: Yes. Partial payments are welcome, and once an account is delinquent, interest accrues only on the remaining balance. Owners 65 or older may also qualify for Tax Relief or Tax Freeze, both applied for in person at the Trustee's office.

faqs.q: How often does Sevier County reappraise?
faqs.a: On a five-year cycle, and this is the year for it. Between cycles a value holds unless the property physically changes. When the new values are set, a certified rate keeps overall collections steady.

faqs.q: Will an unpaid Sevier County tax bill stop a sale?
faqs.a: No, but the balance gets paid out of your sale money because the lien rides with the parcel. Ask the Trustee for the exact payoff on closing day. Once an account reaches Chancery Court it collects costs and can end in a tax sale.
